front: Which gland's disorder decreases mucus secretion to lubricate the vagina during intercourse?
back: Bartholin gland. (Greater vestibular glands secrete mucus for lubrication.)

front: Annual Pap smear screening is recommended to screen for which cancer?
back: Cervical cancer. (Detects precancerous/cancerous cervical changes; may detect HPV.)

front: Breast milk secretion is most directly stimulated by which hormone?
back: Prolactin. (Released by anterior pituitary; stimulates milk production.)

front: A patient presents with galactorrhea. Which diagnostic evaluation should the nurse anticipate?
back: Serum hormone testing. (Workup includes exam + hormone testing ± imaging.)

front: Which hormone is responsible for ovulation?
back: Luteinizing hormone (LH). (LH surge completes follicle maturation → oocyte release.)

front: Male reproductive gland responsible for lubrication (pre-ejaculate) during intercourse?
back: Cowper's gland. (Bulbourethral glands secrete pre-ejaculate to lubricate urethra.)

front: Which male gland produces thick alkaline fluid making up most of seminal fluid?
back: Seminal vesicles. (Produce thick alkaline fluid = majority of ejaculate volume.)

front: Hormone with the major role in testosterone production?
back: Luteinizing hormone (LH) / ICSH. (Stimulates Leydig cells to produce testosterone.)

front: Which hormone decreases secretion of LH (per test bank wording)?
back: Inhibin. (Secreted from Sertoli cells; signals pituitary to slow hormone release.)

front: Priority history question for vaginal discharge with itching + mild dysuria x1 week?
back: "What is the color of the discharge?" (Symptom characterization guides differential.)

front: Term for a woman who has not given birth (regardless of outcome)?
back: Nulliparous.

front: Birth control patch teaching: which statement needs correction?
back: "This type of birth control has a low risk of blood clots." (Patch delivers more estrogen → higher clot risk, especially smokers.)

front: Condom teaching: which statement indicates need for more teaching?
back: "Condoms can be used with oil-based lubricants..." (Oil-based products can damage condoms.)

front: Correct position for breast + axilla palpation during assessment?
back: Supine with arm on side being examined placed under her head.

front: Finding during bimanual exam suggesting PID?
back: Cervical motion tenderness.

front: Male reproductive function teaching: which statement is incorrect?
back: "Alcohol consumption decreases estrogen production." (Alcohol may decrease testosterone and increase estrogen.)

front: Recommended age for males to begin digital prostate examinations (per test bank)?
back: 50 years.

front: Hysteroscopy teaching: which statement indicates need for further teaching?
back: "I will need to be on bedrest for a week..." (Rest at least 2 days, not a week.)

front: Colposcopy teaching: which statement is incorrect?
back: "This test requires general anesthesia." (Typically does NOT require general anesthesia.)

front: Post-laparoscopy teaching: which statement needs correction?
back: "I need to notify the provider if I experience bloating and shoulder pain..." (These can occur from CO₂ and are expected.)

front: Dilation & curettage (D&C) is done primarily to assess what?
back: Endometrial lining. (Endometrial sampling/removal.)

front: Which hormone confirms pregnancy and helps quantify gestational age?
back: Human chorionic gonadotropin (hCG).

front: Older adult female: expected age-related change increases risk for what during intercourse?
back: Painful intercourse (dyspareunia). (↓Estrogen → vaginal atrophy/dryness.)

front: Older adult male GU assessment: expected finding?
back: Atrophy of the penis. (Also: thinner pubic hair, smaller/softer testicles, less elastic scrotum.)

front: Discharge teaching after hysteroscopy: what should be included?
back: Plan to rest the next 2 days before returning to work.

front: After endometrial biopsy: patient reports cramping + light bleeding. Best nurse response?
back: "This is anticipated. Take ibuprofen for discomfort." (Expected; NSAIDs help.)

front: Infertility concern: which medication/supplement could decrease sperm production?
back: Anabolic steroids (supplemental testosterone/anabolics negatively affect sperm production.)

front: Which hormones control the monthly menstrual cycle? (Select-all-that-apply concept)
back: Estrogen, FSH, LH, Progesterone. (Prolactin is for milk secretion.)

front: Normal scrotal assessment findings include what?
back: Darker skin than rest of body; left testicle slightly lower; tiny skin folds (rugae).

front: Which birth control methods increase risk of blood clots?
back: Combination birth control pills, estrogen patch, vaginal ring. (Hormone-releasing methods.)

front: Diaphragm teaching: which points indicate need for further teaching?
back: "99% effective" (actually ~85–95%); "leave in 12 hours" (leave in 6 hours); "antibiotics reduce effectiveness" (that's hormone methods, not diaphragm).

front: Mammogram teaching: what should the nurse include?
back: Avoid deodorant/lotions/creams before test; provider will contact with results (may take a few days).

front: Birth control pills: which personal history prevents use (per test bank item)?
back: History of blood clots and cancer.

front: Which diagnostic studies require NPO beforehand?
back: Laparoscopy and dilation & curettage (D&C).

front: GTPAL: G3 with 2 term births, 0 preterm, 1 abortion at 12 weeks, 2 living = ?
Menstrual cycle control: which pituitary hormones are key?
back: FSH and LH (anterior pituitary).

front: Menstrual cycle control: which ovarian hormones are key?
back: Estrogen and progesterone (ovaries).

front: Scrotum exam: is erythema a normal finding?
back: No. (Normal includes darker skin, left testicle lower, rugae.)

front: Mammogram prep: should the patient remove jewelry? (mammogram vs MRI trick)
back: Not specifically for mammogram. (Jewelry removal is emphasized for MRI; mammogram focus is avoid deodorant/lotions.)

front: Contraception safety: which methods are NOT linked to clot risk (per multi-select item)?
back: Cervical cap and IUD (non-hormone methods in that question's context).
